newsitem.title: USA: Fina Q3 hurt by low refining/chemical margins.
newsitem.headline: Fina Q3 hurt by low refining/chemical margins.

text.p: Fina Inc, fresh from reporting a 13 percent drop in third quarter earnings per share, said its results during the period were hurt by poor profit margins in both its refining and chemicals sectors.

"Third quarter financial results were adversely affected by exceptionally low Gulf Coast refining margins and declining margins in our chemicals product lines," Fina Chief Executive Ron Haddock said in a prepared statement.

Fina, the U.S. unit of Belgium-based Petrofina SA, reported third quarter net income of $38.9 million or $1.25 per share on revenues of $993.3 million compared to $45.0 million or $1.44 a share on revenues of $916.3 million in the year-ago period.
The company, in the latest signal of the booming exploration and production sector of the oil business, said its upstream operations contributed positively to its results.
But on the downstream side, fuels and aromatics production hurt results, the company said.

"The primary cause of reduced earnings in both periods was lower industry Gulf Coast refining margins for fuels and aromatics, which are especially important to the Port Arthur, Texas refinery. Aromatics are a class of petrochemicals often used to raise octane in motor gasoline.
Fina runs the 180,000 barrel per day (bpd) Port Arthur refinery plus a 60,000 bpd refinery in Big Springs, Texas.
